operator_config.name: AddToScheme
operator_config.doc:
AddToScheme adds all types of this clientset into the given scheme. This allows composition
of clientsets, like in:

	import (
	  "k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes"
	  clientsetscheme "k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/scheme"
	  aggregatorclientsetscheme "k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/client/clientset_generated/clientset/scheme"
	)

	kclientset, _ := kubernetes.NewForConfig(c)
	_ = aggregatorclientsetscheme.AddToScheme(clientsetscheme.Scheme)

After this, RawExtensions in Kubernetes types will serialize kube-aggregator types
correctly.

operator_config.name: DefaultFairnessIDLabelLimit
operator_config.doc:
Fairness IDs are populated from a client request header (or an agent-identity
attribute), so their cardinality is not operator-bounded. They label
per-request, flow-control, and plugin metrics; without a cap, every distinct
fairness ID ever observed permanently grows the time series set. The cap
defaults to DefaultFairnessIDLabelLimit and collapses excess values to
OverflowValue. The fallback ID for requests without one is pinned so it stays
visible after the cap fills. A cap of 0 folds every ID, including the
fallback, onto the single overflow series.

operator_config.name: MaxLabelValueLength
operator_config.doc:
MaxLabelValueLength is the longest request-derived label value BoundedLabel
admits. Longer values fold to OverflowValue. Prometheus keeps every admitted
value for the process lifetime and re-serializes it on every scrape, so a
client that sends one multi-megabyte model name would pin that string in
memory and on every scrape.

operator_config.name: OverflowValue
operator_config.doc:
OverflowValue is the label value emitted by BoundedLabel.Bound once the cap
fills. Callers that need to distinguish an "unknown" (empty) request-derived
label value from the cap-overflow value should keep their own sentinel and
gate empty inputs at the wrapper layer.

operator_config.name: ResponseSizeBuckets
operator_config.doc:
ResponseSizeBuckets is a response-body-size histogram ladder from 16 bytes
to 64 MiB. LLM responses span a wider range than request bodies: short
error messages (~100 bytes), non-streaming completions (hundreds of bytes
to a few KiB), and long streaming responses that accumulate token-by-token
(tens of KiB to MiB). The lower floor and tighter mid-range give better
resolution than RequestSizeBuckets for the typical response distribution,
and the 64 MiB ceiling covers very long streamed completions.

operator_config.name: TokenCountBuckets

powers of two (with 1 as the low end and 8 as the second entry). Input
and cached-prompt token histograms across llm-d components share this
shape.

AttributionSourceDerivedRoot means the fairness identity came from the

operator_config.name: AttributionSourceHeader
operator_config.doc:
AttributionSourceHeader means the fairness identity came from the request header.
It does not assert that the header producer was authenticated.

operator_config.doc: FairnessIDHandoffHeader carries the fairness identity EPP resolved to the P/D sidecar.

operator_config.name: FairnessSourceHandoffHeader
operator_config.doc: FairnessSourceHandoffHeader carries where EPP resolved that identity from.

operator_config.name: LogKeySpanID
operator_config.doc: LogKeySpanID is the structured-log field carrying the active span ID.

operator_config.name: LogKeyTraceID
operator_config.doc:
LogKeyTraceID is the structured-log field carrying the active trace ID.
It matches the W3C trace-context identifier used across the llm-d stack
so logs from every component can be queried uniformly by trace.

operator_config.name: otlpProtocolEnv
operator_config.doc: otlpProtocolEnv are the variables that select the OTLP transport, per-signal first.

operator_config.name: ContentTypeJSON
operator_config.doc: ContentTypeJSON is the media type of JSON bodies.

operator_config.name: ContentTypeOptionsNoSniff
operator_config.doc: ContentTypeOptionsNoSniff disables MIME sniffing; http.Error sets it on every body it writes.

operator_config.name: DefaultFairnessID
operator_config.doc:
DefaultFairnessID is the default fairness ID used when no ID is provided in the request.
This ensures that requests without explicit fairness identifiers are still grouped and managed by the Flow Control
system.

operator_config.name: DefaultImageMediaType
operator_config.doc:
DefaultImageMediaType is vLLM's fallback when an Anthropic base64 image
source omits media_type.

operator_config.name: DefaultTenantID
operator_config.doc:
DefaultTenantID prefixes a composed fairness ID for a request that
carries a derived program root but no fairness-ID header. Such traffic
shares one synthetic tenant, so its programs stay addressable as a
group. A gateway stamping this exact tenant string shares the prefix.

operator_config.name: DisaggregatedRevisionHeaderKey
operator_config.doc:
DisaggregatedRevisionHeaderKey carries the selected rollout revision
between phases of a disaggregated request.

operator_config.name: EPPProfileHeaderKey
operator_config.doc:
EPPProfileHeaderKey names the scheduling profile the EPP must run for a
request. The coordinator sets it on every phase call, Envoy routes on it,
and the header-profile-handler reads it.

operator_config.name: FieldBootstrapHost
operator_config.doc:
SGLang bootstrap coordination fields, carried inside kv_transfer_params.
The prefill pod echoes them back so the decode pod can open the bootstrap
channel to it.

operator_config.name: FieldPromptTokenIDs
operator_config.doc:
FieldPromptTokenIDs is the kv_transfer_params field carrying
pre-tokenized prompt token IDs.

operator_config.name: FieldRemoteDecoder
operator_config.doc:
OffloadingConnector P2P tier roles, carried inside kv_transfer_params. The
role is encoded by the nesting key, named for the remote party it
describes: remote_decoder on the prefill request, remote_prefiller on the
decode request, remote_kv_source for a cached-prefix pull. Each block
carries its own kv_request_id.

operator_config.name: FieldResponse
operator_config.doc:
FieldResponse wraps the response object in Responses stream events, which is
where those events carry usage; the Messages message_start event wraps its
object under FieldMessage the same way.

operator_config.name: HeaderContentType
operator_config.doc: HeaderContentType names the HTTP header that carries the media type of a body.

operator_config.name: HeaderContentTypeOptions
operator_config.doc: HeaderContentTypeOptions names the HTTP header that controls MIME sniffing of a body.

operator_config.name: MediaTypeEventStream
operator_config.doc: MediaTypeEventStream is the SSE media type without optional parameters.

operator_config.name: PeerTopologyHeaderKey
operator_config.doc:
PeerTopologyHeaderKey carries the prefill endpoint's encoded topology
from the prefill EPP's response, through the coordinator, to the decode
EPP's request, for topology-affinity-filter and topology-affinity-scorer
running in coordinator deployments.

operator_config.name: PseudoHeaderStatus
operator_config.doc:
PseudoHeaderStatus names the pseudo-header Envoy reports a response's
status in. HeaderStatus is the bare name, which the EPP also accepts.

operator_config.name: ResponsesItemTypeMessage
operator_config.doc:
ResponsesItemTypeMessage is the Responses input item type of a role-tagged
message. An item that omits FieldType is a message too.

operator_config.name: RevisionDecisionIDHeaderKey
operator_config.doc:
RevisionDecisionIDHeaderKey identifies requests that belong to the same
rollout decision. This is needed only for roles such as encode that create
several parallel subrequests from one user request (for example, one per
image). The coordinator must give every subrequest the same value so they
use the same revision.

operator_config.name: RoleAssistant
operator_config.doc: Role values, the strings a message's FieldRole takes.

operator_config.name: ThinkingTypeEnabled
operator_config.doc:
ThinkingTypeEnabled is the Messages thinking.type that carries a budget_tokens
the Anthropic API requires to stay below max_tokens.

operator_config.name: ToolChoiceNone
operator_config.doc: ToolChoiceNone is the tool_choice value that forbids the model from calling a tool.

operator_config.name: encoderPassthroughFields
operator_config.doc:
encoderPassthroughFields are the client fields NewEncoderPrimingBody
forwards: both kwargs fields change preprocessing and feed vLLM's multimodal
hash, so an encoder primed at the deployment default stores its entry under a
hash the prefiller never looks up.

operator_config.name: messagesEncoderPassthroughFields
operator_config.doc:
messagesEncoderPassthroughFields are the fields a Messages body forwards.
vLLM's /v1/messages accepts neither kwargs field, so the prefiller hashes a
Messages image at the deployment defaults and the encoder has to as well.

operator_config.name: fileHydrationPartTypes
operator_config.doc:
fileHydrationPartTypes are the content part types whose FieldFileID names a
Files API upload. A file_id on any other object names no upload the router
would have to hydrate: an annotation on a replayed assistant turn carries one
under a type this map does not hold, so the walk passes over it.

operator_config.name: DataParallelEndpointHeader
operator_config.doc:
DataParallelEndpointHeader is the header name used to indicate the worker <ip:port> for Data Parallel.
Superseded by native data parallel routing in Istio >= 1.28.1, so it keeps its
pre-convention name rather than gaining a second one to remove.

operator_config.name: EncoderEndpointsHeader
operator_config.doc: EncoderEndpointsHeader is the header name used to indicate Encoder workers <ip:port> list

operator_config.name: EndpointPinHeader
operator_config.doc:
EndpointPinHeader carries the worker <ip:port> a request must be scheduled
on. The endpoint-pin-screener keeps only that endpoint.

operator_config.name: FailedStageHeader
operator_config.doc:
FailedStageHeader is the response header the sidecar's disaggregated
handler sets on every response it writes, to the name of the stage that
failed (StageEncode, StagePrefill, or StageDecode). When no stage failed
it carries StageNonePrefilled if the prefill stage completed before the
response was written, and StageNone otherwise. The EPP reads it to charge
a failure to the endpoint that ran the failed stage: a prefill failure
reaches the EPP as the decode endpoint's response status, and without the
header it cannot be told apart from a decode failure. StageNonePrefilled
tells the EPP the prefill endpoint succeeded, which a successful response
alone does not: decode can answer before prefill runs or completes. Only
failures known before the response is written name their stage: prefill
and encode failures, and the concurrent-dispatch decode abort, which
writes the response itself. A decode failure observed after the response
is on the wire carries StageNone or StageNonePrefilled. A sidecar that
predates the header writes no header at all, which tells the EPP it
cannot attribute the status. The sidecar drops any value the model server
set, so only the sidecar marks stages. The EPP strips the header before
the response reaches the client. This comment and docs/disaggregation.md
are the contract; other mentions point here.

operator_config.name: InferencePoolAPIGroup
operator_config.doc: InferencePoolAPIGroup is the InferencePool API group

operator_config.name: KVCachePrefillHeader
operator_config.doc:
KVCachePrefillHeader is the header name used to indicate the prefill worker's
OffloadingConnector P2P tier <ip:port>, the peer a decoder pulls the prompt
KV from. EPP computes the port from the worker's data parallel rank. The
serving address the sidecar connects to stays on PrefillEndpointHeader. It
has no pre-convention alias.

operator_config.name: KVCacheSourceHeader
operator_config.doc:
KVCacheSourceHeader is the header name used to indicate the worker <ip:port>
holding the most cached prefix KV blocks for the request, with its
OffloadingConnector P2P tier port. The same peer travels in the body as
kv_transfer_params.remote_kv_source. It has no pre-convention alias.

operator_config.name: LegacyEncoderEndpointsHeader
operator_config.doc: LegacyEncoderEndpointsHeader is the pre-convention name of EncoderEndpointsHeader.

operator_config.name: LegacyKVCacheSourceHeaders
operator_config.doc:
LegacyKVCacheSourceHeaders are the retired names of KVCacheSourceHeader, from
when it carried the source worker's serving <ip:port>. No component sets or
reads them.

operator_config.name: LegacyPrefillEndpointHeader
operator_config.doc: LegacyPrefillEndpointHeader is the pre-convention name of PrefillEndpointHeader.

operator_config.name: PreferHeader
operator_config.doc:
PreferHeader is the standard HTTP "Prefer" header (RFC 7240). EPP
receives header keys lowercased.

operator_config.name: PreferIfAvailable
operator_config.doc:
PreferIfAvailable is the preference token the coordinator sets to mark a
request as a speculative early-decode attempt: route to a decode worker
only if its KV cache already covers the prompt (at least partially); otherwise EPP surfaces
412 Precondition Failed so the coordinator restarts the pipeline.

operator_config.name: PrefillEndpointHeader
operator_config.doc: PrefillEndpointHeader is the header name used to indicate Prefill worker <ip:port>

operator_config.name: StageEncode
operator_config.doc:
Names of the disaggregated stages, used as the sidecar's stage labels and
as the values carried on FailedStageHeader. StageNone and
StageNonePrefilled are the values a response carries when no stage
failed.

operator_config.name: headerAliases
operator_config.doc:
headerAliases maps each disaggregation header to its pre-convention name. EPP
writes both spellings with the same value, so a sidecar that predates the
rename still routes. Moving an entry from here to retiredNames retires its
old name: EPP stops writing it and the sidecar stops reading it, while both
keep stripping it. Do that once no supported EPP emits the old name.

operator_config.name: retiredNames
operator_config.doc:
retiredNames maps a disaggregation header to names it no longer travels
under. They are stripped wherever the header is stripped, so a client value
cannot reach a sidecar that still reads them, and are never written or read.

operator_config.name: maxObserveBytes
operator_config.doc:
maxObserveBytes caps the copy of a passthrough JSON body kept for the
observer. A body past the cap is forwarded unchanged and not observed; the
usage block of an inference response sits at the end, so a partial copy
cannot be read. A variable so tests can lower it.

operator_config.name: usageKey
operator_config.doc:
usageKey is the JSON key that must be present before a frame can carry usage.
Streamed responses send one frame per token and only the final frame has usage,
so scanning for this is much cheaper than unmarshalling every frame to find out.
The openai and anthropic stream parsers scan for the same word without the
quotes; a JSON serializer always writes the key quoted, so keeping them here
skips more content frames.

operator_config.name: maxValueLen
operator_config.doc:
maxValueLen caps a logged header value. Longer values are truncated so a
verbose metadata header does not dominate the log line.

operator_config.name: BytesPerMB
operator_config.doc: BytesPerMB is the number of bytes in one megabyte.

operator_config.name: DefaultMaxRequestBodySize
operator_config.doc:
DefaultMaxRequestBodySize is the default cap for server.max_request_body_size,
in megabytes. It is generous enough to accommodate multimodal requests that
inline images as data: URIs; text-only deployments can lower it.

operator_config.name: DefaultECConnectorName
operator_config.doc:
DefaultECConnectorName is the EC connector selected when an empty string is
passed to Build. Defaults to ec-shared-storage (no-op on the wire).

operator_config.name: loggerName
operator_config.doc:
loggerName is the WithName scope applied to the context logger in connector
log lines.

operator_config.name: DefaultKVConnectorName
operator_config.doc:
DefaultKVConnectorName is the KV connector selected when an empty string is
passed to Build. Defaults to kv-shared-storage (no-op on the wire).

operator_config.name: loggerName
operator_config.doc:
loggerName is the WithName scope applied to the context logger in connector
log lines.

operator_config.name: maxRedactDepth
operator_config.doc:
maxRedactDepth caps redactStrings recursion so a deeply nested adversarial
body cannot drive it toward the 500-level encoding/json limit on a trace log.

operator_config.name: maxRedactElems
operator_config.doc: maxRedactElems caps how many array elements are kept before a count marker.

operator_config.name: maxRedactRawBodyLen
operator_config.doc: maxRedactRawBodyLen bounds a non-JSON body logged verbatim.

operator_config.name: maxRedactStringLen
operator_config.doc:
maxRedactStringLen is the longest JSON string value kept verbatim; longer
values are replaced with a marker so tensor blobs, base64, and URLs do not
drown out the structural fields.

operator_config.name: maxModelLabelValues
operator_config.doc:
The model_name label is populated from the request body, which no
coordinator config validates against a closed set. Prometheus *Vec types
never evict label combinations, so an unbounded number of distinct model
names would grow the time series set without limit and exhaust memory. The
cap matches EPP's cap for the same reason and for consistency between the
two components.

operator_config.name: CountBuckets
operator_config.doc:
CountBuckets is a small-integer histogram ladder for per-request counts
(encode fan-out, media item inventory).

operator_config.name: ErrorCodePromptTokenMismatch
operator_config.doc:
ErrorCodePromptTokenMismatch is recorded on step_errors_total by the
decode step when prompt_token_parity is "error" and the decode worker
reported a prompt token count different from the rendered one.

operator_config.name: LLMDRouterCoordinatorSubsystem
operator_config.doc:
LLMDRouterCoordinatorSubsystem is the Prometheus subsystem for coordinator
metrics. Every metric declared in this package uses it.

operator_config.name: ModelUnknown
operator_config.doc:
ModelUnknown is the model_name label value for requests that carried no
model in the body (empty or absent). It is distinct from the cardinality
overflow value returned by boundModel once the cap fills.

operator_config.name: parityLabels
operator_config.doc:
parityLabels are model_name, the client's api type and whether the
decode leg carried the rendered token IDs (so a mismatch means the
worker ignored them) or rendered the prompt itself (renderer drift).

operator_config.name: TracerScope
operator_config.doc:
TracerScope is the OTel instrumentation scope for spans emitted by the
coordinator pipeline.

operator_config.name: pipelineSpanName
operator_config.doc: pipelineSpanName is the span covering one run of the step list.

operator_config.name: ErrBadRequest
operator_config.doc:
ErrBadRequest marks a step failure as caused by invalid client input rather
than an internal or upstream fault. Steps wrap it (with %w) when rejecting a
malformed request so the server can answer 400 instead of 502.

operator_config.name: ErrPipelineDone
operator_config.doc:
ErrPipelineDone is returned by a step to signal successful early exit.
The pipeline treats this as success and stops executing further steps.

operator_config.name: inspectedRequestFields
operator_config.doc:
inspectedRequestFields lists the top-level request fields the handler and
the pipeline steps read as Go values; see reqcommon.DecodeRequestBody for why
every other field stays raw. The steps that read messages or input decode
them on use (promptItems).

operator_config.name: validRequestID
operator_config.doc:
validRequestID bounds a client-supplied x-request-id to alphanumerics and
dashes, at most 128 characters. handleInference replaces a header that fails
the match with a generated UUID before it reaches error responses; the
request-logging middleware redacts it. This keeps attacker-controlled content
out of both surfaces.

operator_config.name: StepName
operator_config.doc: StepName is the step's type string in the pipeline config.

operator_config.name: maxTimeoutSeconds
operator_config.doc:
maxTimeoutSeconds is the largest timeout that fits in a time.Duration without
overflowing. Enqueue mode sets no MaxSeconds, so a client value above this
would wrap to a negative or tiny deadline that the producer rejects as a
transport failure.

operator_config.name: unCancelScript
operator_config.value:
redis.NewScript(`
local cancel = redis.call("GET", KEYS[1])
if cancel and cancel == redis.call("GET", KEYS[2]) then
  redis.call("DEL", KEYS[1])
  return 1
end
return 0
`)
operator_config.doc:
unCancelScript revives a cancelled request that is still queued. The
marker is deleted only while it matches the active token, so a marker
left by an older submission of the same id is not cleared by mistake.

operator_config.name: waitBackupPollInterval
operator_config.doc:
waitBackupPollInterval is the slow safety poll under the notify wake-up:
keyspace notifications are fire and forget, so a lost notification is
recovered on the next backup tick rather than never.

operator_config.name: waitPollInterval
operator_config.doc:
waitPollInterval is the poll cadence when the multiplexed wake-up is
unavailable (Redis without keyspace notifications, or wakeup_mode: poll).

operator_config.name: asyncModeEnqueue
operator_config.doc:
asyncModeEnqueue enqueues onto the broker and answers 202 with the
request id.

operator_config.name: asyncModePassthrough
operator_config.doc:
asyncModePassthrough labels the request (objective, fairness id,
quota classification) and lets the pipeline serve it normally.

operator_config.name: asyncModeWait
operator_config.doc:
asyncModeWait enqueues and holds the connection until the result lands
or the wait cap expires (then falls back to the enqueue response).

operator_config.name: defaultModeHeader
operator_config.doc:
defaultModeHeader selects the serving mode when mode_header is not
configured.

operator_config.name: defaultTenantHeader
operator_config.doc: defaultTenantHeader resolves the tenant when tenant_header is not configured.

operator_config.name: defaultTimeoutHeader
operator_config.doc:
defaultTimeoutHeader carries a per-request deadline when timeout_header is
not configured.

operator_config.name: defaultWaitMaxSecs
operator_config.doc:
defaultWaitMaxSecs bounds client-requested wait deadlines when no
max_seconds is configured: every wait holds a live connection, so an
arbitrarily large requested deadline must not pin one for days.

operator_config.name: resultKeyPrefix
operator_config.doc:
resultKeyPrefix scopes the per-request result keys the async processor
delivers to; see resultKey.

operator_config.name: resultFetchGraceTTL
operator_config.doc:
resultFetchGraceTTL is the default mailbox expiry applied after a
successful fetch delivery, overridable via fetch_grace_seconds. The full
result TTL exists for the completion-to-first-fetch window, which is
client paced. After a delivered fetch, retention only covers lost-response
retries, which fire within seconds, so the key is shrunk to this grace
window instead of lingering for the full TTL.

operator_config.name: statusClientClosedRequest
operator_config.doc: statusClientClosedRequest is 499 Client Closed Request (nginx convention).

operator_config.name: validAsyncRequestID
operator_config.doc:
validAsyncRequestID mirrors the server's x-request-id validation, so the
fetch routes accept exactly the ids the inference path can produce.

operator_config.name: errCacheMiss
operator_config.doc:
errCacheMiss signals that the conditional-decode cache probe returned 412.
It flows from the proxy's ModifyResponse to its ErrorHandler, which swallows
it so the miss can fall through to the rest of the pipeline.

operator_config.name: defaultForceStreamBufferSize
operator_config.doc:
defaultForceStreamBufferSize is the budget applied when force_stream is on but
force_stream_buffer_size is unset. 1GiB of buffered responses is negligible on
a node that runs GPU inference, so an operator overrides it only to tune.

operator_config.name: defaultForceStreamMaxRequestBytes
operator_config.doc:
defaultForceStreamMaxRequestBytes caps one forced request's reservation when
force_stream_max_request_size is unset. 256KiB holds roughly 16k output tokens
for a single choice, enough for a large reply while keeping one request from
claiming a large share of the shared budget. It is a fixed size rather than a
fraction of the budget: the cap bounds a single reply, not a slice of the
aggregate. Capped to the budget when that is smaller.

operator_config.name: errForceStreamCeiling
operator_config.value: errors.New("force-stream: buffered response exceeded its reserved budget")
operator_config.doc:
errForceStreamCeiling marks a forced request aborted because its buffered
response exceeded the bytes reserved for it, usually a per-token byte estimate
that came up short rather than a pod ignoring the limit. Nothing was written to
the client, so the decode step falls back to the pass-through (recording
error_ceiling) rather than failing a conforming reply.

operator_config.name: errForceStreamLossyFrame
operator_config.value: errors.New("force-stream: stream carried data the reassembler drops; falling back to pass-through")
operator_config.doc:
errForceStreamLossyFrame marks a stream that carried data the reassembler does
not fold: a chat delta field beyond role and content (reasoning, tool_calls,
refusal), a choice or frame field outside the folded set (token_ids returned
alongside text, routed_experts, prompt_token_ids), a non-text Messages block, or
a choice index past the declared n. forceStreamLossy diverts a request that
declares such a feature up front, but a server-side default (a reasoning parser,
routed experts) emits these with no request-side signal. Detecting it on the
frame falls back to the pass-through, which preserves the data, rather than
dropping it from a forced reply. Nothing has reached the client, so it is
handled like errForceStreamUnreadable.

operator_config.name: errForceStreamOversize
operator_config.value: errors.New("force-stream: responses reply exceeded its reserved budget; falling back to pass-through")
operator_config.doc:
errForceStreamOversize marks a Responses forced reply whose terminal frame did
not fit even the reservation plus the request body size, the allowance that
covers the generated text plus the request fields (tools, instructions, schema,
metadata) a terminal frame echoes. A frame past that carries bytes neither
accounts for, a coordinator estimate miss rather than a pod fault. Nothing has
reached the client, so the decode step falls back to the pass-through rather
than failing a reply the pod returned intact.

operator_config.name: errForceStreamTruncated
operator_config.value: errors.New("force-stream: upstream stream ended before a terminal marker")
operator_config.doc:
errForceStreamTruncated marks a forced stream that ended with a clean EOF before
any terminal marker: no data: [DONE] line and no shape terminal (a Responses
terminal event or a choice finish_reason). The reassembly would look complete
but omit the cut-off tail, so the request falls back to the pass-through rather
than return a truncated reply as a 200. It is handled like errForceStreamUnreadable.

operator_config.name: errForceStreamUnreadable
operator_config.value: errors.New("force-stream: upstream stream unreadable; falling back to pass-through")
operator_config.doc:
errForceStreamUnreadable marks a forced request whose upstream returned 200 but
a stream the coordinator could not parse or read before any bytes reached the
client. The non-forced pass-through may serve it from a different pod code path,
so the decode step falls back to it rather than failing. The underlying parse or
read error is logged where this is returned, so the fallback stays diagnosable.

operator_config.name: forceStreamBaseOverheadBytes
operator_config.doc:
forceStreamBaseOverheadBytes covers the top-level envelope shared by every
reply: id, model, created, object, and the usage block.

operator_config.name: forceStreamBytesPerToken
operator_config.doc:
forceStreamBytesPerToken is the per-token byte unit the reservation and the
ceiling both derive from, so a response that honors its token limit is never
aborted and an upstream that ignores it still trips the ceiling. It bounds the
two encodings a token can take. As text it spans a few code points at up to
four UTF-8 bytes each, so 16 is an upper bound with margin. As a generate-shape
token id it bounds the id's JSON encoding (decimal digits and a separator),
which stays under 16 bytes for any realistic vocabulary. Because the
reservation uses this same unit, the generate ceiling trips at the token limit
regardless of the exact per-id width.

operator_config.name: forceStreamMaxFrameBytes
operator_config.doc:
forceStreamMaxFrameBytes is the upper bound on one SSE line for the chunk
shapes, whose per-request reservation is usually smaller and binds first.
Streaming chunks are small (one token delta), so this rejects a single
malformed or oversized frame rather than a whole reply.

operator_config.name: forceStreamPerChoiceOverheadBytes
operator_config.doc:
forceStreamPerChoiceOverheadBytes covers one choice's JSON envelope (its
index, finish_reason, and message or text keys) so a request asking for
many short completions still reserves enough for their structure.

operator_config.name: forceStreamScanStartBytes
operator_config.doc:
forceStreamScanStartBytes is the SSE scanner's initial buffer size; it
grows as needed toward the per-request frame cap.

operator_config.name: streamOnlyHeaders
operator_config.doc:
streamOnlyHeaders describe the event stream the forced request read rather than
the reply that replaces it: its framing, length, encoding and caching. The
forced reply sets its own Content-Type and Content-Length.

operator_config.name: thinkingTypeDisabled
operator_config.doc:
thinkingTypeDisabled is the Anthropic Messages thinking.type that turns
thinking off; enabled and adaptive both let the model emit thinking blocks.

operator_config.name: maxGRPCFrameBytes
operator_config.doc:
maxGRPCFrameBytes bounds individual upstream gRPC stream frames read by
coordinator steps.

operator_config.name: batchedInt64MetadataFields
operator_config.doc:
batchedInt64MetadataFields are the placeholder-metadata fields the rebuild
can encode: batched int64 keep_on_cpu fields, the image_grid_thw and
video_grid_thw shapes the Qwen-VL family uses. A field outside the set has
no known layout, so its metadata is left to the worker via content_parts.

operator_config.name: vllmRawViewExt
operator_config.doc:
vllmRawViewExt is the msgpack extension type vLLM's MsgpackEncoder uses for
the inline bytes of a small tensor (CUSTOM_TYPE_RAW_VIEW in
vllm/v1/serial_utils.py).

operator_config.name: ParamForceStream
operator_config.doc:
ParamForceStream opts the decode step into force-streaming: a
non-streaming client request is sent upstream with stream enabled, and
the streamed response is reassembled into one non-streaming reply.

operator_config.name: ParamForceStreamBufferSize
operator_config.doc:
ParamForceStreamBufferSize is the total byte budget, as a human-readable
string ("1GiB"), shared across concurrent forced requests. A request that
cannot reserve its estimate from it takes the non-buffering pass-through.

operator_config.name: ParamForceStreamMaxRequestSize
operator_config.doc:
ParamForceStreamMaxRequestSize caps the bytes one forced request may
reserve for its generated reply, as a human-readable string ("256KiB"). It
keeps a single large request from claiming a large share of the shared
budget and starving concurrent candidates. Unset defaults to 256KiB (room
for roughly 16k output tokens), capped to force_stream_buffer_size when that
is smaller. A Responses request also reserves its own body size from the
shared budget, outside this cap, for the request fields its reply echoes.

operator_config.name: ParamForwardPromptTokenIDs
operator_config.doc:
ParamForwardPromptTokenIDs, when true, makes decode and conditional-decode
send the rendered token IDs in kv_transfer_params.prompt_token_ids on
text-only chat completions, Responses and Messages requests. The decode
worker builds the engine input from them and skips chat templating and
tokenization. Requires vLLM v0.27.0 or later, where earlier versions
ignore the field, and a render step, which the pipeline builder checks.
Defaults to false.

operator_config.name: ParamPromptTokenParity
operator_config.doc:
ParamPromptTokenParity selects what the decode and conditional-decode
steps do when the worker's usage reports a prompt token count different
from the rendered one: "off" skips the check, "warn" (default) counts and
logs it, "error" also records a step error. The response to the client
is never changed.

operator_config.name: mmPayloadNone
operator_config.doc:
mmPayloadNone omits the tensors. Generate-format encode requests carry
the client's media as content_parts, and prefill sends features with
mm_metadata when it has metadata and EC coverage for every entry, else
the client's media as content_parts.

operator_config.name: mmPayloadTensors
operator_config.doc: mmPayloadTensors ships the processed tensors as kwargs_data.

operator_config.name: audioFormatMIME
operator_config.doc:
audioFormatMIME maps OpenAI's input_audio.format values to one canonical MIME
each, for the allowlist check validateInlineAudio runs. "wav" and "mp3" match
OpenAI's chat-completions API; the rest cover formats backends commonly accept.
coordinator.yaml's allowed_audio_content_types comment records what one MIME
per format means for an operator narrowing that list.

Each value must be a bare lowercase type, since validateInlineAudio hands it
straight to allowedContentTypeForModality's equality match
(TestAudioFormatMIMEValuesAreNormalized).

operator_config.name: cgnatBlock
operator_config.doc:
cgnatBlock is the RFC 6598 carrier-grade NAT range, which net.IP has no
dedicated predicate for.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxDownloadSize
operator_config.doc: defaultMaxDownloadSize is the default cap for max_download_size, in megabytes.

operator_config.name: errBlockedAddress
operator_config.value: fmt.Errorf("address resolves to a blocked range: %w", pipeline.ErrBadRequest)
operator_config.doc:
errBlockedAddress marks a dial to a forbidden address. It wraps
pipeline.ErrBadRequest so the connection failure surfaced by http.Client.Do
(wrapped in *url.Error/*net.OpError, both of which Unwrap) classifies as a
client 4xx rather than a 502.

operator_config.name: ipv4CompatBlock
operator_config.doc: ipv4CompatBlock is the deprecated IPv4-compatible range ::/96 (RFC 4291).

operator_config.name: maxRedirects
operator_config.doc: maxRedirects matches the net/http default, which a custom CheckRedirect drops.

operator_config.name: nat64Block
operator_config.doc:
nat64Block is the RFC 6052 well-known NAT64 prefix; the low 32 bits carry
the IPv4 destination.

operator_config.name: perModalityContentTypeParams
operator_config.doc:
perModalityContentTypeParams names the config keys overriding the built-in
MIME allowlist per modality. A slice, for the reason on
perModalityDownloadSizeParams.

operator_config.name: perModalityDownloadSizeParams
operator_config.doc:
perModalityDownloadSizeParams names the config keys overriding
max_download_size per modality. A slice, not a map, so a config with more
than one bad value reports the same one on every restart.

operator_config.name: sglangPrefillGrace
operator_config.doc:
sglangPrefillGrace limits how long a concurrent prefill stream may linger
after decode has already finished. A variable so tests can shorten it.

operator_config.name: sglangPrefillWaitOnTerminal
operator_config.doc:
sglangPrefillWaitOnTerminal bounds how long decode waits for prefill's
cached_tokens frame or trailing status before finishing the stream.
A variable so tests can widen it under race-detector load.

operator_config.name: fieldMetrics
operator_config.doc:
fieldMetrics is the per-request metrics object vLLM sets on the final
include_usage chunk, and on the non-streaming reply, when the server runs
with --enable-per-request-metrics or speculative decoding.

operator_config.name: generateContentPartTypes
operator_config.doc:
generateContentPartTypes maps a modality to its /inference/v1/generate
content_parts type.

operator_config.name: maxErrorBodySize
operator_config.doc:
maxErrorBodySize caps how much of a non-2xx upstream response body is read
into memory, bounding OOM exposure to an adversarial upstream pod.

operator_config.name: DefaultScorerWeight
operator_config.doc: DefaultScorerWeight is the weight used for scorers referenced in the configuration without explicit weights.

operator_config.name: defaultProfileName
operator_config.doc:
defaultProfileName names the profile ensureSchedulingLayer creates when the
config defines none.

operator_config.name: defaultCrossReplicaSyncInterval
operator_config.doc:
defaultCrossReplicaSyncInterval is the fallback cadence at which local
per-endpoint state is pushed to the syncer when none is configured.

operator_config.name: RequestHandlingProducerLayer
operator_config.doc: RequestHandlingProducerLayer holds DataProducers in DataProducerPhaseRequestHandling.

operator_config.name: RequestHeaderLayer
operator_config.doc:
RequestHeaderLayer holds RequestHeaderProcessors, which run after request
assembly and before flow control admission.

operator_config.name: ScreenerLayer
operator_config.doc: ScreenerLayer holds screeners, which run between the two DataProducer phases.

operator_config.name: ErrDuplicateExtractorType
operator_config.value: errors.New("duplicate extractor type configured for the same source")

operator_config.name: ErrNoDefaultProducer
operator_config.value: errors.New("no default producer found for missing data key")

operator_config.name: ErrUnresolvedDataKeys
operator_config.value: errors.New("required data keys remain unproduced after default producer resolution")

operator_config.doc: compile-time type assertion

operator_config.name: activePortsAnnotation
operator_config.doc:
activePortsAnnotation is used to specify which ports on a pod should be considered
as active for inference traffic. The value should be a comma-separated list of port numbers.
Example: "8000,8001,8002"

operator_config.name: errPoolNotSynced
operator_config.value: errors.New("InferencePool is not initialized in data store")

operator_config.name: errRegistrationDropped
operator_config.value: errors.New("endpoint registration dropped: collector already registered or failed to start")
operator_config.doc:
errRegistrationDropped reports an endpoint that could not be tracked: its collector is
still registered from an earlier registration (an upsert overlapping an in-flight delete)
or failed to start. Callers match it with errors.Is to decide whether to retry.

operator_config.name: ErrFlowIDEmpty
operator_config.doc: ErrFlowIDEmpty indicates that a flow specification was provided with an empty flow ID.

operator_config.name: ErrFlowInstanceNotFound
operator_config.doc: ErrFlowInstanceNotFound indicates that a requested flow instance (a `ManagedQueue`) does not exist.

operator_config.name: ErrInvalidQueueItemHandle
operator_config.doc:
ErrInvalidQueueItemHandle indicates that a QueueItemHandle provided to a SafeQueue operation (e.g.,
SafeQueue.Remove()) is not valid for that queue, has been invalidated, or does not correspond to an actual item in
the queue.

operator_config.name: ErrPriorityBandNotFound
operator_config.doc: ErrPriorityBandNotFound indicates that a requested priority band does not exist in the registry configuration.

operator_config.name: ErrQueueItemNotFound
operator_config.value: errors.New("queue item not found for the given handle")
operator_config.doc:
ErrQueueItemNotFound indicates that a SafeQueue.Remove(handle) operation did not find an item matching the
provided, valid QueueItemHandle. This can occur if the item was removed by a concurrent operation.

operator_config.name: defaultEnqueueChannelBufferSize
operator_config.doc: defaultEnqueueChannelBufferSize is the default size of a worker's incoming request buffer.

operator_config.name: defaultEvictionConfirmationGrace
operator_config.doc:
defaultEvictionConfirmationGrace covers the reclaiming stage (engine abort, KV GC, scrape,
staleness window) for the default utilization detector. Deployments pairing eviction with the
concurrency detector can lower it substantially.

operator_config.name: defaultEvictionConfirmationTimeout
operator_config.doc:
defaultEvictionConfirmationTimeout bounds how long an unconfirmed revocation can hold the
reclamation pacing gate closed.

operator_config.name: defaultExpiryCleanupInterval
operator_config.doc: defaultExpiryCleanupInterval is the default frequency for scanning for expired items.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxRevocationsPerDecision
operator_config.doc:
defaultMaxRevocationsPerDecision caps revocations per reclamation decision, bounding the
damage from mean-footprint misestimation.

operator_config.name: defaultNoEndpointRequestTTL
operator_config.doc:
defaultNoEndpointRequestTTL is the queue-wait budget applied while the candidate pool has no endpoints when
neither budget is configured. It is deliberately equal to `defaultRequestTTL`, so splitting the budget is opt-in:
sizing the two regimes apart (a cold start is minutes, a time-to-first-token SLO is seconds) is a
deployment-specific decision, not one a default can make.

operator_config.name: defaultRequestTTL
operator_config.doc:
defaultRequestTTL is the default Time-To-Live applied to queued requests when the configuration
does not specify one. It is a queue-wait budget: a request still undispatched after this long is
shed with a retryable backpressure signal instead of being served with severely degraded
time-to-first-token. With no client or gateway deadline (the well-lit guides configure no gateway
request timeout) it is the only bound on waiting against a pool that has endpoints; where such
deadlines exist and fire sooner, context cancellation evicts the request first.

operator_config.name: ErrProcessorBusy
operator_config.doc:
ErrProcessorBusy is a sentinel error returned by the processor's Submit method indicating that the processor's
internal buffer is momentarily full and cannot accept new work.

operator_config.name: maxCleanupWorkers
operator_config.doc:
maxCleanupWorkers caps the number of concurrent workers for background cleanup tasks. This prevents the processor
from overwhelming the Go scheduler with too many goroutines.

operator_config.name: PriorityQueueName
operator_config.doc:
PriorityQueueName identifies the priority queue implementation (used for benchmark labels).

This queue provides a concurrent-safe priority queue whose ordering is maintained by an internal
container/heap. Items are ordered by the configured OrderingPolicy, with the highest-priority
item (per the policy) at the head.

Each item's position in the heap is tracked on its handle, enabling O(log n) targeted removal.

operator_config.name: DefaultBandSelectionPolicyRef
operator_config.doc: DefaultBandSelectionPolicyRef is the default policy for ordering priority bands within a dispatch cycle.

operator_config.name: DefaultFairnessPolicyRef
operator_config.doc: DefaultFairnessPolicyRef is the default policy for selecting which flow's queue to service next.

operator_config.name: DefaultOrderingPolicyRef
operator_config.doc: DefaultOrderingPolicyRef is the default policy for selecting items within a single flow's queue.

operator_config.name: DefaultUsageLimitPolicyRef
operator_config.doc: DefaultUsageLimitPolicyRef is the default policy to compute usage limit of a priority band dynamically.

operator_config.name: defaultFlowGCTimeout
operator_config.doc:
defaultFlowGCTimeout is the default duration of inactivity after which an idle flow is garbage collected.
This also serves as the interval for the periodic garbage collection scan.

operator_config.name: defaultPriorityBandGCTimeout
operator_config.doc:
defaultPriorityBandGCTimeout is the default duration of inactivity after which a dynamically provisioned
priority band is garbage collected. Set to 2x flow GC timeout to ensure flows are cleaned up first.

operator_config.name: defaultPriorityBandMaxBytes
operator_config.doc:
defaultPriorityBandMaxBytes is the default byte-size capacity for a priority band if not explicitly
configured. It is set to 1 GB.

operator_config.name: defaultPriorityBandMaxRequests
operator_config.doc:
defaultPriorityBandMaxRequests is the default request-count capacity for a priority band if not
explicitly configured. Together with the default request TTL (60s), it only binds when a band's
arrival rate under a dispatch halt exceeds maxRequests/TTL (~83 req/s); below that, TTL expiry
bounds occupancy first.

operator_config.name: ErrContextCancelled
operator_config.doc:
ErrContextCancelled indicates a request was evicted because its associated context (from
`FlowControlRequest.Context()`) was cancelled. This error typically wraps the underlying `context.Canceled` or
`context.DeadlineExceeded` error.

operator_config.name: ErrEvicted
operator_config.doc:
ErrEvicted is a sentinel error indicating a request was removed from a queue *after* being successfully enqueued,
but for reasons other than successful dispatch (e.g., TTL expiry, displacement). Errors returned by
`FlowController.EnqueueAndWait()` that signify post-queue eviction will wrap this error.

Callers should use `errors.Is(err, ErrEvicted)` to check for this general class of failure.

operator_config.name: ErrFlowAtCapacity
operator_config.doc: ErrFlowAtCapacity indicates that only the flow's own maxRequestsPerFlow or maxBytesPerFlow limit blocked admission.

operator_config.name: ErrFlowControllerNotRunning
operator_config.doc:
ErrFlowControllerNotRunning indicates that an operation could not complete or an item was evicted because the
`controller.FlowController` is not running or is in the process of shutting down.

When returned by `FlowController.EnqueueAndWait()`, this will be wrapped by `ErrRejected` (if rejection happens
before internal queuing) or `ErrEvicted` (if eviction happens after internal queuing).

operator_config.name: ErrNoEndpoints
operator_config.doc:
ErrNoEndpoints indicates that a request was rejected at the queue-capacity boundary while the candidate pool had no
endpoints. The queue acts as a scale-from-zero waiting room; when it fills with no backends to drain it, the
rejection reflects genuine unavailability rather than backpressure against a contended pool.

operator_config.name: ErrQueueAtCapacity
operator_config.doc: ErrQueueAtCapacity indicates that a request could not be enqueued because queue capacity limits were met.

operator_config.name: ErrRejected
operator_config.doc:
ErrRejected is a sentinel error indicating a request was rejected by the `controller.FlowController` *before* being
formally enqueued. Errors returned by `FlowController.EnqueueAndWait()` that signify pre-queue rejection will wrap
this error.

Callers should use `errors.Is(err, ErrRejected)` to check for this general class of failure.

operator_config.name: ErrTTLExpired
operator_config.doc: ErrTTLExpired indicates a request was evicted from a queue because its effective Time-To-Live expired.

operator_config.name: ModalityNone
operator_config.doc: ModalityNone is the mm.modality value when no multimodal content is present.

operator_config.name: ModalityOther
operator_config.doc:
ModalityOther is the metric label value for a modality outside image, audio
and video.

operator_config.name: prefixFieldSeparator
operator_config.doc: prefixFieldSeparator ends each written field so adjacent fields cannot run together.

operator_config.name: DecisionsPathSuffix
operator_config.doc: DecisionsPathSuffix identifies the Decisions API.

operator_config.name: SystemOnePathSuffix
operator_config.doc: SystemOnePathSuffix identifies the System One decisions API.

operator_config.name: BytesPerToken
operator_config.doc:
BytesPerToken is the average number of request bytes per prompt token, used
to estimate token counts without a tokenizer. The tokenizer's estimate
backend packs this many bytes into each pseudo-token, so its counts agree
with byte-based estimates.

operator_config.name: UploadedMediaHeadBytes
operator_config.doc:
UploadedMediaHeadBytes bounds how many leading bytes of a media payload are
retained for container sniffing: the parser captures this many bytes of an
uploaded file part, and the estimator's dimension and duration walks read
within it.

operator_config.name: ErrCoordinationUnsupported
operator_config.value: errors.New("the cross-replica syncer does not support GetOrSet")
operator_config.doc:
ErrCoordinationUnsupported is returned by GetOrSet from a CrossReplicaSyncer
that cannot provide linearizable request-level state across replicas.

operator_config.name: ErrIncompatiblePriorityType
operator_config.value: errors.New("incompatible priority score type for comparison")
operator_config.doc:
ErrIncompatiblePriorityType indicates that a FairnessPolicy attempted to compare items from two different flow
queues whose ItemComparators have different ScoreType values, making a meaningful comparison impossible.

operator_config.name: DefaultStalenessThreshold
operator_config.doc:
DefaultStalenessThreshold defines the built-in threshold for considering data as stale.
If a request's data has not been read/written within this duration, it is reaped in the next
cleanup cycle. It applies when no process-wide override is set via SetDefaultStalenessThreshold.

operator_config.name: defaultCleanupInterval
operator_config.doc: defaultCleanupInterval defines the periodic interval that the cleanup goroutine uses to check for stale data.

operator_config.name: defaultStalenessThreshold
operator_config.doc:
defaultStalenessThreshold is the process-wide default staleness threshold applied to new
PluginState instances. It may be overridden once at startup via SetDefaultStalenessThreshold.

operator_config.name: DefaultProducerRegistry
operator_config.doc:
DefaultProducerRegistry maps a data key to the default producer plugin name (same as type).
Populated via RegisterAsDefaultProducer.

operator_config.name: PluginsWithPluginDependencies
operator_config.doc: PluginsWithPluginDependencies maps plugin types to their configuration parser function, used to determine plugin dependencies

operator_config.name: Registry
operator_config.doc: Registry is a mapping from plugin type to Factory function.

operator_config.name: RegistryMetadata
operator_config.doc: RegistryMetadata maps a plugin type to its PluginMetadata.

operator_config.name: ErrNotFound
operator_config.doc: ErrNotFound is the not found error message.

operator_config.name: StabilityAlpha
operator_config.doc: StabilityAlpha indicates an experimental plugin with no backwards-compatibility guarantees.

operator_config.name: StabilityBeta
operator_config.doc: StabilityBeta indicates a feature-complete plugin following the +2 minor release deprecation policy.

operator_config.name: StabilityStable
operator_config.doc: StabilityStable indicates a production-grade plugin guaranteed to be backwards compatible.

operator_config.name: ConditionalDecodeHandledAttributeKey
operator_config.doc:
ConditionalDecodeHandledAttributeKey is the request-attribute key a
PreRequest plugin sets when it has evaluated the "Prefer: if-available"
preference for a request. The director consults this after PreRequest
plugins run: a conditional-decode request that no plugin claimed is
rejected with 412 so misconfigurations (gate plugin forgotten) surface as a
fast fallback rather than a silent forward.

operator_config.name: DataProducerPhaseRequestHandling
operator_config.doc:
DataProducerPhaseRequestHandling runs the producer during request
handling, on the located endpoints before screeners, so screeners can
consume its data.

operator_config.name: DataProducerPhaseScheduling
operator_config.doc:
DataProducerPhaseScheduling runs the producer on the screened endpoints
before admission and scheduling.

operator_config.name: RequestHandlingDataProducerExtensionPoint
operator_config.doc:
RequestHandlingDataProducerExtensionPoint names DataProducers that run in
DataProducerPhaseRequestHandling.

operator_config.name: TerminationCauseClientDisconnect
operator_config.doc:
TerminationCauseClientDisconnect is a stream torn down under the EPP while the response was
in flight. A client disconnect is the most common reason; any teardown the EPP observes only
as a cancelled stream (Envoy drain or restart, an upstream reset, the EPP's own drain)
produces the same value, because the EPP cannot distinguish the reasons from its side of
the stream.

operator_config.name: TerminationCauseError
operator_config.doc:
TerminationCauseError is a stream that ended without completing for any reason not otherwise
classified: a half-close that reaches the EPP before its cancellation propagates, or an
EPP-side failure.

operator_config.name: TerminationCauseEvicted
operator_config.doc: TerminationCauseEvicted is a stream the EPP terminated to reclaim capacity.

operator_config.name: TerminationCauseNatural
operator_config.doc:
TerminationCauseNatural is a stream the model server ended on its own, including responses
that deliver an error status in full.

operator_config.name: TerminationCauseNotObserved
operator_config.doc:
TerminationCauseNotObserved is a request whose route skips response processing: the EPP
stops processing the stream after routing and never sees the response.

operator_config.name: Affinity
operator_config.doc:
Affinity indicates a scorer that prefers endpoints with existing locality, such as kv-cache or session-related state,
and therefore tends to give higher scores to the same endpoints.

operator_config.name: Balance
operator_config.doc: Balance indicates a scorer that its preference is balanced between Affinity and Distribution.

operator_config.name: Distribution
operator_config.doc:
Distribution indicates a scorer that prefers spreading requests evenly across all candidate endpoints to avoid
hotspots and improve overall utilization.

operator_config.name: EngineTypeLabelKey
operator_config.doc: EngineTypeLabelKey is the Pod label used to identify the inference engine type.

operator_config.name: InFlightLoadDataKey
operator_config.doc:
InFlightLoadDataKey carries the per-endpoint in-flight load snapshot used by
load-aware scorers. Populated by InFlightLoadProducer.Produce on each
candidate endpoint at the start of every scheduling cycle.

Represents the live, real-time load on the endpoint (tokens and requests),
injected dynamically and never overwritten during a scheduling cycle.

operator_config.name: UncachedRequestTokensDataKey
operator_config.doc:
UncachedRequestTokensDataKey carries the projected impact of the current request
on a specific endpoint. Populated statically during scheduling.

operator_config.name: DCGMExtractorType
operator_config.doc: DCGMExtractorType is the plugin type for the DCGM metrics extractor.

operator_config.name: GPUUtilizationDataKey
operator_config.doc:
GPUUtilizationDataKey identifies per-endpoint GPU utilization published
by the DCGM extractor and consumed by the generic endpoint-attribute
filter and scorer.

operator_config.name: TTFTPercentilesDataKey
operator_config.doc:
TTFTPercentilesDataKey carries the per-endpoint TTFT summary the
latency-observation-scorer-hub reads, published by the latency-observer-producer-hub.

operator_config.name: MetricsExtractorType
operator_config.doc:
MetricsExtractorType is the plugin type for the core metrics extractor,
which publishes the custom scalar metric attributes.

operator_config.name: MultiClusterKVCacheUtilizationKey
operator_config.doc: MultiClusterKVCacheUtilizationKey holds a pool's aggregate KV-cache utilization.

operator_config.name: MultiClusterQueueSizeKey
operator_config.doc: MultiClusterQueueSizeKey holds a pool's aggregate waiting-queue size.

operator_config.name: NixlFailedNotificationsKey
operator_config.doc: NixlFailedNotificationsKey holds the failed KV cache notifications.

operator_config.name: NixlFailedTransfersKey
operator_config.doc: NixlFailedTransfersKey holds the failed KV cache transfers.

operator_config.name: NixlKVExpiredRequestsKey
operator_config.doc: NixlKVExpiredRequestsKey holds the requests whose KV cache expired before it was read.

operator_config.name: EncoderCacheMatchInfoKey
operator_config.doc:
EncoderCacheMatchInfoKey is attached to endpoints by the multimodal data
producer and consumed by scorer/latency plugins that need encoder-cache locality.

operator_config.name: P2PSourceDecisionDataKey
operator_config.doc:
P2PSourceDecisionDataKey identifies the decision a p2p-source-producer
instance reached for the request in PreRequest.

operator_config.name: PrefixHashSetDataKey
operator_config.doc:
PrefixHashSetDataKey carries the cross-replica recent-window of prefix block
hashes this EPP believes an endpoint holds. Used by approx-prefix-cache-producer
when a CrossReplicaSyncer is configured.

operator_config.name: ReusablePrefixTokensDataKey
operator_config.doc:
ReusablePrefixTokensDataKey identifies the request-wide reusable prefix
token floor published by a p2p-source-producer instance.

operator_config.name: SpeculativeTierKey
operator_config.doc:
SpeculativeTierKey is the CachedBlocksByTier key for speculative index
entries, which carry no engine-reported device tier.

operator_config.name: SessionIDDataKey
operator_config.doc:
SessionIDDataKey identifies the session identifier published on the request
attribute store. The default producer is the session-id-producer.

operator_config.name: TopologyAttributeKey
operator_config.doc: TopologyAttributeKey identifies the Topology attribute stored on each endpoint.

operator_config.name: TopologyExtractorType
operator_config.doc: TopologyExtractorType is the plugin type identifier for the topology extractor.

operator_config.name: DefaultStateTTL
operator_config.doc:
DefaultStateTTL is how long a peer value counts after it was last
refreshed, when the syncer's stateTTL is unset.

operator_config.name: MinimumDuration
operator_config.doc:
MinimumDuration is the shortest duration a syncer accepts in its
configuration.

operator_config.name: errMessageTooLarge
operator_config.doc: errMessageTooLarge reports a message over maxMessageBytes.

operator_config.name: handshakeTimeout
operator_config.doc: handshakeTimeout bounds the setup of one incoming connection.

operator_config.name: keepaliveTime
operator_config.doc:
A connection whose peer acknowledges nothing for keepaliveTime plus
keepaliveTimeout is closed and redialed. 10s is the shortest client
keepalive time gRPC allows.

operator_config.name: maintenanceInterval
operator_config.doc:
maintenanceInterval paces peer link reconciliation, heartbeats and
expiry of peer values.

operator_config.name: maxMessageBytes
operator_config.doc:
maxMessageBytes bounds one message in both directions. Values that do
not fit in one message are split across several.

operator_config.name: maxPeers
operator_config.doc:
maxPeers bounds the peer replicas whose values one replica holds at once
and the connections it accepts.

operator_config.name: maxStreamsPerConnection
operator_config.doc:
maxStreamsPerConnection bounds the streams open on one connection. A peer
keeps one stream open and opens the next when it ends. With maxPeers and
maxMessageBytes it bounds the messages a replica receives at once.

operator_config.name: publishStream
operator_config.doc:
publishStream is the one RPC between replicas: a stream of messages from
the replica that dials to the replica that listens.

operator_config.name: sendQueueLimit
operator_config.doc:
sendQueueLimit and maxQueuedBytes bound the messages queued for one
peer. Messages beyond either are dropped; each value is resent within
refreshInterval.

operator_config.name: MultiClusterPluginType
operator_config.doc: MultiClusterPluginType discovers peer clusters as endpoints for a cluster-scoped EPP.

operator_config.name: AttributeProducerType
operator_config.doc: AttributeProducerType is the plugin type for the endpoint attributes producer.

operator_config.name: KVCacheUsagePercentKey
operator_config.doc: --- Internal Keys (for Legacy/Gauge Usage) ---

operator_config.name: LoraInfoRunningAdaptersMetricName
operator_config.doc: LoRA metrics based on MSP

operator_config.name: defaultEngineName
operator_config.doc: defaultEngineName is the default engine used when defaultEngine is not specified.

operator_config.name: DefaultEngineType
operator_config.doc: DefaultEngineType is the key for the fallback mapping.

operator_config.name: DefaultEngineTypeLabelKey
operator_config.doc: DefaultEngineTypeLabelKey is the default label on Pods that indicates the inference engine type.

operator_config.name: MultiClusterMetricsExtractorType
operator_config.doc: MultiClusterMetricsExtractorType reads only a pool's aggregate metrics, not engine metrics.

operator_config.name: addQuotesRE
operator_config.doc: addQuotesRE is the compiled form of the pattern used by addQuotesToLabelValues.

operator_config.name: labelPairRE
operator_config.doc:
labelPairRE handles structural parsing: extracts the key, operator, and
value from a key="value" or key!="value" label matcher (after
addQuotesToLabelValues normalisation). Field validation (label name syntax)
is delegated to model.LegacyValidation.IsValidLabelName.

operator_config.name: metricSpecRE
operator_config.doc:
metricSpecRE handles structural parsing: extracts the metric name token and optional label block.
Field validation (metric name syntax) is delegated to model.LegacyValidation.IsValidMetricName.

ModelExtractor is not a requesthandling.DataProducer as data here is produced
asynchronously and not tied to incoming requests

operator_config.name: podGVK
operator_config.doc: podGVK is the core/v1 Pod GVK watched by the pod notification handler.

operator_config.name: baseTransport
maxIdleConnections
operator_config.doc:
the maximum idle connection count is shared by all endpoints. The value is
set high to ensure the number of idle connection is above the expected
endpoint count. Setting it too low would cause thrashing of the idle connection
pool and incur higher overheads for every GET (e.g., socket initiation, certificate
exchange, connections in timed wait state, etc.).

operator_config.name: maxIdleConnsPerHost
operator_config.doc:
allow some grace when connections are not made idle immediately (e.g., parsing
and updating might take some time). This allows maintaining up to two idle connections
per endpoint (defined as scheme://host:port).

operator_config.name: defaultStepTimeout
operator_config.doc:
defaultStepTimeout bounds each Poll and each Extract independently so a slow
extractor cannot starve sibling extractors of their tick budget.

operator_config.name: maxDumpSubscribers
operator_config.doc: maxDumpSubscribers bounds the DumpState payload on large deployments.

operator_config.name: maxResponseBytes
operator_config.doc:
maxResponseBytes caps the metrics payload read from one scrape, so a hostile or broken
model server cannot exhaust memory in the parser.

operator_config.name: sampleSuffixes
operator_config.doc:
sampleSuffixes are the suffixes of histogram and summary samples, which the text parser files
under the base family. Counters are declared under their _total name and need no suffix.

operator_config.name: MultiClusterMetricsDataSourceType
operator_config.doc:
MultiClusterMetricsDataSourceType scrapes like the pod metrics source. A distinct type
lets a config pair it with the multicluster extractor, separate from the pod pipeline.

operator_config.name: defaultMultiClusterScheme
operator_config.doc:
defaultMultiClusterScheme is https, not the pod source's http: a cross-cluster scrape
crosses a trust boundary, so it is encrypted and verified by default.

operator_config.name: EndpointNotificationSourceType
operator_config.doc: EndpointNotificationSourceType is the plugin type identifier for endpoint notification sources.

operator_config.name: NotificationSourceType
operator_config.doc: NotificationSourceType is the plugin type identifier for k8s notification sources.

operator_config.name: StrictBandSelectionPolicyType
operator_config.doc: StrictBandSelectionPolicyType is the registration type for the strict band selection policy.

operator_config.name: SheddableFilterType
operator_config.doc:
SheddableFilterType only admits sheddable requests (priority < 0) into the eviction queue.
This uses the project-wide definition of sheddable from requtil.IsSheddable.

operator_config.name: PriorityThenTimeOrderingType
operator_config.doc:
PriorityThenTimeOrderingType evicts the lowest priority request first,
breaking ties by newest dispatch time (least KV-cache investment).

operator_config.name: GlobalStrictFairnessPolicyType
operator_config.doc: GlobalStrictFairnessPolicyType is the registration type for the global strict fairness policy.

operator_config.name: enqueueTimeAttributeKey
operator_config.doc:
enqueueTimeAttributeKey is the per-request attribute under which Pick
stashes the flow-control enqueue timestamp for PreRequest to read back.

operator_config.name: RoundRobinFairnessPolicyType
operator_config.doc: RoundRobinFairnessPolicyType is the registration type for the round-robin fairness policy.

operator_config.name: WeightedFairShareFairnessPolicyType
operator_config.doc: WeightedFairShareFairnessPolicyType is the registration type for this policy.

operator_config.name: EDFOrderingPolicyType
operator_config.doc:
EDFOrderingPolicyType is the registration type for the EDF ordering policy.

It selects the request with the earliest absolute deadline.
For detailed documentation, see README.md.

operator_config.name: FCFSOrderingPolicyType
operator_config.doc:
FCFSOrderingPolicyType is the registration type for the FCFS ordering policy.

It selects the item with the earliest logical enqueue time.
For detailed documentation on behavior and queue pairing, see README.md.

operator_config.name: SLODeadlineOrderingPolicyType
operator_config.doc:
SLODeadlineOrderingPolicyType is the registration type for the SLO deadline ordering policy.

It selects the request with the earliest SLO-based deadline.
For detailed documentation, see README.md.

operator_config.name: sloTtftHeader
operator_config.doc: sloTtftHeader is the request header name for SLO time-to-first-token in milliseconds.

operator_config.name: MaxSaturationDetectorType
operator_config.doc: MaxSaturationDetectorType is the unique identifier for this plugin.

operator_config.name: defaultConcurrencyMode
operator_config.doc: defaultConcurrencyMode is used when ConcurrencyMode is unset.

operator_config.name: defaultFailOpen
operator_config.doc: defaultFailOpen is used when FailOpen is unset.

operator_config.name: defaultHeadroom
operator_config.doc: defaultHeadroom is the default burst allowance (0%).

operator_config.name: defaultMaxConcurrency
operator_config.doc: defaultMaxConcurrency is the safe baseline for many LLM serving engines.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxTokenConcurrency
operator_config.doc: defaultMaxTokenConcurrency is the default maximum number of tokens allowed per endpoint.

operator_config.name: modeHybrid
operator_config.doc: modeHybrid uses endpoint average saturation across both request and token counts.

operator_config.name: modeRequests
operator_config.doc: modeRequests uses request count for concurrency detection.

operator_config.name: modeTokens
operator_config.doc: modeTokens uses token count for concurrency detection.

operator_config.name: DefaultKVCacheUtilThreshold
operator_config.doc: DefaultKVCacheUtilThreshold is the default KV cache utilization (0.0 to 1.0) threshold.

operator_config.name: DefaultMetricsStalenessThreshold
operator_config.doc:
DefaultMetricsStalenessThreshold defines how old metrics can be before they are considered
stale.

operator_config.name: DefaultQueueDepthThreshold
operator_config.doc: DefaultQueueDepthThreshold is the default waiting queue size threshold.

operator_config.name: StalenessIgnore
operator_config.doc:
StalenessIgnore excludes endpoints with missing or stale metrics from the saturation
average. When every candidate endpoint is stale, the pool scores 0.0 and dispatch continues,
consistent with the Filter's fail-open fallback. Deployments choose this posture when the
availability cost of a metrics collection outage outweighs the risk of driving stale,
possibly overloaded endpoints.

operator_config.name: StalenessSaturated
operator_config.doc:
StalenessSaturated scores endpoints with missing or stale metrics as fully saturated
(1.0). A fleet-wide metrics collection failure therefore halts dispatch entirely rather than
admitting blind.

operator_config.name: defaultHeadroom
operator_config.doc: defaultHeadroom is the default burst allowance (0%).

operator_config.name: UtilizationDetectorType
operator_config.doc: UtilizationDetectorType is the unique identifier for this plugin.

operator_config.name: staleWarnInterval
operator_config.doc:
staleWarnInterval bounds how often the detector logs about endpoints with missing or stale
metrics. Saturation is evaluated every dispatch cycle (~1ms), so the condition must be logged
on a time budget, never per evaluation.

operator_config.name: domainExplicit
operator_config.doc: domainExplicit uses operator-supplied priority anchors, interpolating missing priorities by priority value and clamping outside the anchor range.

operator_config.name: domainRank
operator_config.doc: domainRank maps by ordinal rank, ignoring numerical priority values.

operator_config.name: domainValue
operator_config.doc: domainValue maps proportionally to numerical priority values.

operator_config.name: shapeLinear
operator_config.doc:
shape constants define the interpolation curve applied across the ceiling range.
Only "linear" is supported; additional shapes (sigmoid, exponential, step, etc.) may be added.

operator_config.name: PolicyType
operator_config.doc: PolicyType is the registration type for the priority holdback usage limit policy.

operator_config.name: PolicyType
operator_config.doc:
PolicyType is the registration string. The YAML "type:" field in
pluginsCustomConfig must equal this value for the loader to find the
factory.
compile-time validation

operator_config.name: Type
operator_config.doc: Type is the registered plugin type for the probabilistic admitter.
compile-time interface assertion

operator_config.name: TracerScope
operator_config.doc:
TracerScope is the OTel instrumentation scope shared by all plugins under
the requesthandling framework component.

operator_config.name: ApproxPrefixCachePluginType
operator_config.doc: ApproxPrefixCachePluginType is the default producer type for PrefixCacheMatchInfoDataKey.

operator_config.name: nodeNil
operator_config.doc:
nodeNil is the prev/next sentinel. newHashLRU keeps capacity at or below it,
so node indexes stay below it.

operator_config.name: MultiClusterPluginType
operator_config.doc: MultiClusterPluginType is the explicit cluster-scoped approx-prefix producer.

operator_config.name: indexUpdateStateKey
operator_config.doc:
indexUpdateStateKey identifies the per-request record of indexer entries
PreRequest added. The record lives until the response arrives so a failed
response can remove the entries.

operator_config.name: minBlockSizeTokens
operator_config.doc:
minBlockSizeTokens is the floor applied to the block size returned by
GetBlockSize. The routing-side indexer keeps one LRU entry per (pod, block),
so very small block sizes cause gigabyte-scale memory growth at scale. 64
tokens is coarse enough to bound memory while still preserving useful
prefix-match signal. Defined as a var so tests in this package can lower it
to exercise prefix-match logic at small block sizes without leaking a knob
into the public configuration surface. See
https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/1158.

operator_config.name: defaultBlockSizeTokens
operator_config.doc:
defaultBlockSizeTokens is the default token block size. It equals
minBlockSizeTokens so an unset value does not trigger the below-minimum
override and its startup warning.

operator_config.name: defaultLRUCapacityPerServer
operator_config.doc:
defaultLRUCapacityPerServer is the default capacity of the LRU indexer per server.
The indexer is an approximation to the actual prefix LRU cache state on the model servers per server (pod).
A small capacity ensures a high accuracy of cache hit on the model server, but it will
increase the chance of false negatives. A high capacity does the opposite.
Each entry is one router block, so at defaultBlockSizeTokens the default covers
31250 * 64 = 2,000,000 tokens per server.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxPrefixBlocks
operator_config.doc:
defaultMaxPrefixBlocks is the fallback block cap, consulted only when
MaxPrefixTokensToMatch is 0 and MaxPrefixBlocksToMatch is non-zero; the
default token cap otherwise supersedes it.
Two long requests with the same prefix up to this limit will be indistinguishable.
This parameter provides a trade-off between cache size, prefix matching speed and matching
accuracy. Use a small value if most requests are short to reduce cache size and speed up the
matching process. Use a large value if most requests are long to increase the matching accuracy.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxPrefixTokens
operator_config.doc:
defaultMaxPrefixTokens caps prefix matching at the context window of large
production models (128K tokens, e.g. gpt-oss 120b), a reasonable upper bound
that covers the long-prompt use cases seen in production. It takes precedence
over defaultMaxPrefixBlocks: maxBlocks = defaultMaxPrefixTokens / blockSizeTokens.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxSyncedTokens
operator_config.doc:
defaultMaxSyncedTokens caps the recent-window published per endpoint when
cross-replica sync is enabled. Sized to the default per-pod index
(defaultLRUCapacityPerServer blocks × defaultBlockSizeTokens) so one
replica can publish a full index's worth of recent hashes for an endpoint.

operator_config.name: experimentalDefaultPrefillProfile
operator_config.doc:
experimentalDefaultPrefillProfile is a hardcoded profile name for prefill nodes.
In P/D disaggregation mode, the prefill and decode are usually represented as two different
scheduling profiles to pick the prefill and decode endpoints. This constant defines the
prefill profile name to ensure that the index is updated for the prefill endpoint and not
only for the primary endpoint that will initially handle the request.
This is hardcoded for now until we land on a canonical approach for plugins to identify
prefill and decode endpoints (See https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api-inference-extension/issues/2080)

operator_config.name: podActiveCheckInterval
operator_config.doc: podActiveCheckInterval is the interval at which we check if pods are still active.

operator_config.name: unlimitedPrefixBlocks
operator_config.doc:
unlimitedPrefixBlocks is the block cap used when both MaxPrefixTokensToMatch
and MaxPrefixBlocksToMatch are 0. Prompt length is already bounded by the
model server's context window, so an absent cap matches at most one context
window of tokens.

operator_config.name: produceTimeoutMargin
operator_config.doc:
produceTimeoutMargin is added to the window so the director's per-producer
timeout does not cancel a request still waiting for its batch to seal.

operator_config.name: PluginType
operator_config.doc: PluginType is the unique identifier for the burst prefix cache producer plugin.

operator_config.name: balanceByRequests
operator_config.doc: balanceByRequests balances placement by request count (the default).

operator_config.name: balanceByTokens
operator_config.doc:
balanceByTokens balances placement by prefix-block (token) load, charging a
prefix only the blocks a replica must still prefill - blocks already held from
an earlier request sharing that prefix are free. Spreads long-prompt requests
so no replica saturates on stacked prefixes while shorter ones pack together.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxPrefixBlocks
operator_config.doc:
defaultMaxPrefixBlocks caps how many leading blocks form a group key.
Two prompts identical up to this many blocks are treated as one group.

operator_config.name: maxWindowDurationMs
operator_config.doc:
maxWindowDurationMs bounds the batch window. Every request waits up to this
long, so a misconfigured large value is rejected at construction rather than
stalling every request.

operator_config.name: unlimitedBatchSize
operator_config.doc:
unlimitedBatchSize is the MaxBatchSize sentinel that disables the
per-window cap on accumulated requests.

operator_config.name: unlimitedPerReplica
operator_config.doc:
unlimitedPerReplica is the MaxPerReplica sentinel that disables the
per-replica cap, sending every sample of a group to a single replica.

operator_config.name: InFlightLoadProducerType
operator_config.doc: InFlightLoadProducerType is the default producer type for InFlightLoadDataKey.

operator_config.name: LongOutputTokens
operator_config.doc:
LongOutputTokens is the flat output-token estimate for a LONG (reasoning)
request. It is deliberately a fixed value rather than the client's
thinking_budget: the estimate exists to rank requests by load, where the
LONG-vs-SHORT separation dominates, not to predict exact length.

operator_config.name: ShortOutputTokens
operator_config.doc:
ShortOutputTokens is the flat output-token estimate for a SHORT
(tool-call) request.

operator_config.name: UnknownOutputTokens
operator_config.doc:
UnknownOutputTokens is the output-token estimate for an UNKNOWN request
(no output-length signal) until the first UNKNOWN completion is observed.

operator_config.name: unknownOutputWindow
operator_config.doc:
unknownOutputWindow bounds the running average's divisor, so each UNKNOWN
observation weighs at least 1/unknownOutputWindow and the estimate follows
workload shifts.

operator_config.name: LatencyObserverProducerType
operator_config.doc:
LatencyObserverProducerType is the plugin type of the producer that observes
per-endpoint time-to-first-token and publishes the percentile anchors the
latency-observation-scorer-hub reads.

operator_config.name: LatencyObserverProducerType
operator_config.doc: LatencyObserverProducerType is the plugin type of this producer.

operator_config.name: dispatchStateKey
operator_config.doc:
dispatchStateKey names the per-request record written in PreRequest and
read back when the first response chunk arrives.

operator_config.name: inflightStateKey
operator_config.doc:
inflightStateKey names the per-request in-flight readings Produce takes
for every candidate, which PreRequest narrows to the winner.

operator_config.name: maxDebugDumpEndpoints
operator_config.doc: maxDebugDumpEndpoints bounds the DumpState payload on large deployments.

operator_config.name: ProducedKey
operator_config.doc: ProducedKey is the data key emitted by this producer.

operator_config.name: ProducerType
operator_config.doc: ProducerType is the type name used to register the multimodal data producer.

operator_config.name: bytesPerImage
operator_config.doc: bytesPerImage is the assumed memory per tracked image.

operator_config.name: defaultCacheSizeInMB
operator_config.doc: defaultCacheSizeInMB is 4 GiB (4096 MiB).
